title: Quiet portfolio and manager briefing draft
content:
Quiet portfolio — manager brief (prep)

One-line ask:
- Align on prioritization of two customer-facing hiring programs and one internal calibration initiative; ask for a short runway (3 sprints) and explicit tradeoff (capacity vs hiring acceleration).

Top signals (concise evidence I want to convey):
- Hiring funnel: reduced offer-to-accept velocity by ~18% since Aug 2025 (see OPS-789 for candidate timeline heatmap). Key drag = interview scheduling and panel fatigue.
- Calibration uplift: ran 6 cross-functional calibration sessions with eng + PMs; post-calibration variance in score down from 1.6 -> 0.9 (sample: 32 hires). Anecdotes saved in Confluence-4521.
- Ops runway: automated interview scheduling pilot cut coordinator time by ~7h/week across team; needs full rollout to see 30%+ ROI. PR: people-ops#314.

Stories to tell (two crisp examples):
1) Candidate rescue story (Nov 2025): Senior infra candidate had slipped due to panel mismatch; I coordinated a condensed panel + hiring timeline reprioritization, converted to offer within 10 days. Impact: avoided losing a high-fit hire and preserved momentum for dedicated infra roadmap. Evidence: candidate notes & timeline in CONFLUENCE-4521, calendar snapshots.
2) Calibration -> product launch velocity (Dec 2025): After running calibration with product and eng leads, a later hire was rated more consistently and onboarded into a cross-team project that shipped 3 weeks earlier. Result: measurable reduction in ramp variance; qualitative praise from Eng Director.

Risks & mitigations (what I expect manager to help unblock):
- Risk: Leadership bandwidth to commit to 2 more calibration sessions this quarter.
  Mitigation: propose 45-min focused sessions and use short pre-read, not full slides.
- Risk: Tooling rollout timelines vs. hiring needs.
  Mitigation: If automation rollout slips, request temporary contractor budget or re-prioritize interview panels.

Concrete asks (what I want from this 1:1):
- Quick read + greenlight to run two targeted calibration sessions (Jan/Feb).
- Decision on reallocation of one FTE from general ops to hiring acceleration for 3 months.
- Coaching: how to frame this as "risk mitigation for hiring velocity" when talking to Eng Directors.

Draft talking points (short):
- "I have three signals that show we can materially improve hiring velocity with a small allocation of focused time and one temporary headcount."
- "This is about reducing lost candidate momentum and lowering interview fatigue for our hiring managers."
- "If we can run a lightweight pilot on tool rollout + two calibration sessions, we should be able to show measurable wins within 8–12 weeks."

90-day checklist (what I will do if approved):
- Week 1–2: confirm sessions, invite list, and short pre-read.
- Week 3–6: run sessions + implement 2 quick changes to panel structure. Track candidate timelines.
- Week 7–12: full rollout of the scheduling automation to two teams; measure coordinator hours saved and offer velocity.

Signals I will track (metrics):
- Median offer-to-accept time (days) — baseline & weekly.
- Interview-to-offer conversion by role.
- Coordinator hours saved per week.
- Calibration score variance (inter-rater standard deviation).

Open questions (notes to self):
- Would an explicit "bandwidth pledge" from Eng Dir (1 hour/month) be more persuasive than asking for a temporary FTE?
- Should I draft a one-pager for the Exec-brief deck or keep to manager + hiring managers first?

Closing sentence (for manager 1:1):
- "I want to deliver low-friction changes that protect hiring momentum — can I run a short pilot and come back with results in 8 weeks?"

Notes to self: keep examples crisp, avoid too much process detail in the first ask, and surface the ROI early. Leave detailed timelines and links for follow-up only if manager asks.

Revision log:
- 2025-11-03: initial notes and raw timeline.
- 2025-12-15: added candidate rescue story and metric baselines.
- 2026-02-12: updated ask to include temporary FTE option and added linked artifacts.
